evidence: Caragiannis, Hemaspaandra, and Hemaspaandra define standard Dodgson via adjacent swaps to a strong Condorcet winner and standard Young via deletions to a weak Condorcet winner.
Courtin, Mbih, and Moyouwou prove that with three alternatives Dodgson and Young always select the same winner and state that the theorem fails beyond three alternatives.
Brandt, Dong, and Peters independently place Dodgson and Young in the same three-candidate maximin-equivalence class.
Approximation literature establishes the computational difficulty and conceptual distinction of the two distance notions, but not the exact first small-profile layer.

value.rationale: Dodgson and Young use two canonical but different notions of distance to Condorcet consensus. Because their exact equivalence for three candidates is now established, the first four-candidate layer is a natural structural boundary. The exact \(7/96\) incidence, universal refinement direction, and seven symmetry classes provide a complete and interpretable first separation.
